title: User | thepilotnews.com - Southern Louisiana Homeowners Are Shifting Roofing Preferences - Here's How That Affects New Roof Installation Costs
text:
roof installation - Daigle Roofing and Construction Daigle Roofing and Construction discusses regional material trends and their impact on installation pricing JENNINGS, La. - Roofing preferences in Southern Louisiana have shifted noticeably in recent years, with more homeowners in and around Jennings requesting metal roofing and upgraded shingle systems instead of the standard three-tab asphalt shingles that once dominated the region. Daigle Roofing and Construction says this shift is changing the conversation homeowners have about new roof installation costs, since material choice now plays a larger role in the final price than it once did.
Historically, most homes in the area were roofed with basic asphalt shingles chosen primarily for affordability. Today, many homeowners are weighing longer-term durability against upfront cost, particularly given the region's exposure to heat, humidity and tropical storm activity. Metal roofing, once considered a premium option reserved for commercial buildings, has become increasingly common on residential homes throughout Southern Louisiana due to its wind resistance and extended lifespan.
This trend affects installation pricing directly, since material remains one of the largest cost variables in any new roof project. A basic asphalt shingle roof typically costs less upfront than a standing-seam metal roof, but the total project price also depends on roof size, the pitch and complexity of the roofline, whether a tear-off of the existing roof is required, the condition of the decking underneath, and the type of underlayment installed.
Roof size continues to be the baseline factor in any estimate, since larger homes require more material and labor regardless of which roofing system is chosen. However, contractors report that homeowners are increasingly asking about long-term value rather than simply the lowest upfront price, which has shifted more installations toward architectural shingles and metal systems even though both carry higher material costs than basic shingles.
Tear-off requirements also factor into current project costs. Many homes being reroofed today are 20 years or older and were originally built with a single layer of asphalt shingles, meaning a full tear-off is often necessary to properly install newer, heavier-duty materials. Decking condition frequently comes into play here as well, since older wood decking exposed to years of Gulf Coast humidity sometimes requires repair or replacement before new roofing can go on.
Roof pitch and underlayment choices round out the primary cost factors. Steeper or more complex rooflines require additional labor time regardless of material, and homeowners upgrading to metal or premium shingle systems are also increasingly opting for higher-performance underlayment to maximize the lifespan of their investment.
"We're seeing more homeowners think about their roof as a long-term investment instead of just the next repair," said the owner of Daigle Roofing and Construction . "That means material choice has become one of the biggest factors in what a new roof actually costs."
Because of these shifting preferences, the range of new roof installation costs in Southern Louisiana has widened. A basic asphalt shingle replacement on a simple roofline remains one of the more affordable options, while a metal roof installation involving a full tear-off, decking repairs and upgraded underlayment sits at the higher end of the pricing spectrum. Homeowners are encouraged to weigh both the upfront cost and the expected lifespan of each material when planning a project.
Daigle Roofing and Construction says the best way for homeowners to navigate these choices is to request a detailed, itemized estimate that breaks down material costs separately from labor, tear-off and underlayment, allowing for a direct comparison between different roofing systems rather than a single bottom-line number.
